assets.statement: L1 ("all positive integers are sums of ≤3 2-full numbers") refuted by n=7: powerful ≤7 are {1,4}, 3-term sums miss 7 (also n=15); canonical "large" hedge is load-bearing, so any close needs an explicit threshold/exception set.

no explicit mathematical sentence stated on the node so all twelve attacks return no target; per D0 the machine-verified counterexample stands on record, and repair requires restating L1 as a concrete sentence with explicit witnesses and range before any route can close

k=1 endpoint counterexample on A=ℕ (F=X−1>X^{1/2}) plus prior sampled-to-universal defect (A={2^n} only); repair requires ∃k(a,ε) quantifier order and a ∀A proof of the chosen-k bound; R007 remains without a quantitative engine.
Counterexample N=3, A={1,2}: sums 3,4,5,6 distinct, but |A|=2 > √3; any repaired bound must be cube-root-type counting, which still cannot close branch A's asymptotic.
positive upper density does not imply positive natural density (explicit block-set counterexample); repair: prove a uniform lower bound |S_C∩[1,N]| ≥ δN for all large N, never a limsup.

Witness A={2^k} has a zero subsequence of (1_A*1_A)(n)/log n, so the nonzero-limit quantifier fails; any repair must prove a two-sided Θ(log n) bound for all sufficiently large n, not merely boundedness or a subsequence estimate.
